# 2 Baruch Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Fall of Jerusalem

---

**1** "Blessed is the one who was not born, or he who having been born has died.

**2** But as for us the living, woe to us, because we see the afflictions of Zion and what has befallen Jerusalem.

**3** I will call up the sirens from the sea, and you night-spectres come from the desert, and you demons and jackals from the forests: wake and gird your loins for mourning and take up with me a lamentation.

**4** And do not mourn for me, O Zion; mourn for yourself, O Zion; for the desolation of the Comforter who was near you.

**5** For the righteous have been taken away and the prophets have gone to sleep, and we have gone forth from our land and Zion has been taken from us, and we have nothing now save only the Mighty One and his law.

**6** If therefore we put away from our hearts all our vanity and direct our heart to the Mighty One, he will restore to us again all that we have lost, and multiply it for us many times.

**7** But the righteous of these days, whose righteousness is their portion, they shall rejoice and not be ashamed.

**8** And those whose fathers have been taught wisdom shall receive their wages, and those who have been ruled by men of understanding shall not be removed.

**9** But now we are called by this name which we had inherited from our fathers, and yet we have become estranged from our inheritance.

**10** What therefore shall we say to those who are at rest in Babylon, or to those who have been scattered there?

**11** For Zion has been taken from us, and we have no place of refuge.

**12** And we have left our land, and we have no inheritance now in other lands.

**13** Now, O brides, do not enter the bridal chambers; and O virgins, weave not your garlands; and O wives, pray not for children;

**14** And you who are with child, pray not that you may be delivered; for the barren shall rather rejoice, and those who have no sons shall exult, and those who have sons shall be grieved.

**15** For why should men beget children, if they are to be given over to Sheol?

**16** Or why should the human race continue, if it is to come to destruction?

**17** Or why should man rule over his household, if he is to be bereaved?

**18** Or why should there be travail in giving birth, if the fruits of the womb are to be cut off before they are ripe?

**19** Or why should one put on the splendor of virginity, or adorn himself with beauty, when it is destined to be brought to naught in Sheol?"

---

*LOGOS notes: Ch 10 is Baruch's great lament, echoing Job 3 (v.1), Jer 20 (v.14 "cursed is he who was born"), and the dirge genre of Lamentations. Vv.13-14 mirror the eschatological childbirth reversal of Mk 13:17. "Sheol" preserved untranslated.*
